notes.text: The cited comparison is a close continuous witness to the narrative. The specific work behind Heilprin’s short citation is considered separately.
Four parasangs and the tannin are shared. The Meil Tzedakah parallel has a bridge like Heilprin, while the Folkmasa transcription prints an eagle. Preserve Heilprin’s reading.
Five days and the cloud agree with the close parallel.
The closest parallel also gives each person an additional seventy years. This is the ending reported within the tale.
The first-person עמי and the second-person suffixes belong to the stranger’s speech, as in the close narrative parallel.
The first-person assurance is speech to be relayed through the angel. Swearing by the divine name belongs to the preceding speech by the angel, describing Shefifon’s adjuration.
Job’s wording is quoted directly in the tale, including in the close parallel.

The Bavli’s reading of the Samuel verse provides the close interpretive parallel, while Heilprin gives it as part of the tale.
